analysis:
Examined both CLI-reference excerpts and the supplied change map/partial patch. The visible addition at docs/provider/cli-reference.md:156 (head) exposes an operator-facing addon status/hold/release command. The patch's new section at head:904 describes an owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to the live process identity and a separate add-on socket. Documentation alone does not establish an authorization bypass or availability regression.

Reviewed surrounding descriptions of model switching and usage settlement (head:329–390), provider/account credential separation (head:102–108), encrypted cache storage (head:66–88), and existing daemon environment, watchdog, key and helper configuration (base:1726–1951). No supplied change demonstrates weakened encryption, account cache scoping (T-041), serving authorization/revocation (T-052/T-053), artifact qualification (T-054), or privileged fan authority (TB-010). Existing documented limitations are not new findings.

Integration must examine AddonCommand.swift, lifecycle-mailbox dispatch and the add-on socket implementation together: verify owner/process binding, bounds and expiry for holds, cleanup after client/process failure, and interaction with memory admission, idle unloading (T-029), cancellation (T-010), model switching and terminal usage settlement. The remainder of the added command documentation and the changed head:1758 content are not replayed here; the patch is truncated. These coverage limits prevent a security conclusion about the new hold-control behavior, rather than proving a missing control.
